supersededBy: docs/SPEC.md reflects these, including the notes that override a pick (e.g. finals dropped, searchResults resolved by searchHover).

answers.question: Seat alerts without an account
answers.note: i'm not sure if this needs to be a day one feature, but hey if it works and we can test that it does and that people can come to rely on it, hey that's fine. consider that we might need to check if someone's already signed up for this alert, etc. and undoing the alert should require confirmation.

answers.question: Adding a block of time
answers.note: both for sure. we don't need location, etc. the user can worry about that and i don't want to be prefilling all these things etc. it's fine as is. i just think the blocks would be nice mostly as a thing to see extra stuff you'd have and to restrict the searching.

answers.question: Can you hide the sidebar?
answers.note: even simplier then an extra collapse button at the bottom, just allow the user to click the same icon again to hide it. ie. search is selected, clicking search again means everything's collapsed.

answers.question: Course colors
answers.note: should also allow for the user to change the color of the course just for fun, maybe just as simple as clicking on the color circle icon in the courses views and it having a little tooltip to select from a good amount of predefined colors.

answers.question: Comparing two plans
answers.note: note this as a future feature, but i don't feel like it's necessary rn and the UX is a bit tricky.

answers.question: Density
answers.note: lots of info here, dense is better.

answers.question: Header when you drill into a course
How much we explain the estimates
Search filters
answers.note: kind of none of the above. i like the UX of something that has one line under the search bar with a chip/dropdown thing for the different things you could filter by. for example, "gen-eds" "credits" "fits my plan" etc. once it's set it changes color to show it's actively applying.

answers.question: Where final exams show up
answers.picked: Only in Problems and course details
answers.recommended: A Finals view on the calendar
answers.note: let's actually do neither. final exams can be rescheduled if you have overlapping ones, and the university takes care in making sure that they usually don't overlap. and that's one extra data source to worry about, and final exam times aren't even usually released until a few weeks into a semester. let's not do that.

answers.question: Your very first visit
answers.note: oh shit i actually really fuck with this numbered overview of how the app works as a good introduction. good thinking. i like this more than my previous thought about the blank thing with "start from scratch" or "generate". but maybe adding in a callout to the generate thing as an alternate thing, or idk. just consider that too.

answers.question: Name of the first sidebar tab
Sections that don't fit
answers.note: label only for now is fine, again with allowing some dynamism, maybe someone prefers to see something overlapping so then they go and pick something else for the one it overlaps with, etc. it's not a great deal. maybe a little note next to the sections label like "0 fit" or "2 fit", idk.

answers.question: Showing how fresh seat counts are
Automatic schedule suggestions
answers.note: i think generating things would be a good feature to have from the start. but think about the user stories more... i think generating them would mostly be separate from being inside of any specific plan. maybe it could be another option when you select the plus button for a new plan? it could allow you to add multiple plans. and on a fresh session (i don't want a marketing page or anything; just throw people in), it could just show two options to start from scratch or to generate. make this feature as excellent as the rest of this schedule builder, please. and i'm not sure i wanna use the sparkles anywhere for this since it's just using algorithms and whatnot. sparkles for actual LLM stuff only please.

answers.question: How other sections appear when you open a course
answers.note: i'm partial to dashed outlines; though some courses have a *ton* of sections and i'm a bit worried about how this will display. i really like the idea behind the dashed outlines though, and it's a good visual to see all the options in front of you.

answers.question: Grade distribution
answers.note: i like the bars. consider that we use +/- grades too. planet terp does combined bars for those with different segments for A-, A, and A+ within the same A bar. i like that. they also have A, B, C, D, F, W, and other. W means withdrawl, btw, but people know that.

answers.question: Instructor information
answers.note: i think i prefer this cards thing, actually. there's usually not more than a handful of professors for the class, so it's useful to see all that extra information right at thet top, i feel.

answers.question: Connection details
answers.picked: A small map of the walk
answers.recommended: Two bars: time you have vs time you need
answers.note: YES to the map omg that'd look so cool. i'd prefer only doing this if we're able to display the actual route between the things that the user would really take, not a straight line because that makes it seem like our calculation is a straight line. and i think the GIS thing takes into account routing because we have the accessible path option. also: please call it the accessible option, or accessible whatever, and not "step-free".

answers.question: What the phone version opens to
answers.note: i don't want us to have to worry about a specific mobile implementation for every new feature we add, but i do think supporting mobile would be a good thing. i've seen other apps built with shadcn have their sidebar turn into a sort of drawer thing from the bottom that's able to be at halfway or expand up, etc. i think this would be the best thing to do for now, and it sort of just requires working on the shell of the sidebar and things like that.

answers.question: How overlapping classes look
answers.note: no red outline necessary. yes it's a problem but i feel like it's a pretty common thing for users to have different options displayed like that, so we shouldn't necessarily yell at them for it always. for instance, say i have two socy 4xx classes at the same time i'm deciding between now. it's kind of mute which one i pick when it comes to the mechanics of my schedule. i just want to see that i could do both and not be yelled at. sure, it's a problem to be highlighted, but it's sort of well understood.

answers.question: Where problems live
answers.picked: Problems tab + count in top bar
answers.recommended: Tab + banner in the course list
answers.note: don't yell at the user with that extra box. again, problems might show up when the user is still figuring out their schedule. that's okay.

answers.question: Quick calls
picked: Show a Saturday column only when a plan has a Saturday class
Show full sections (labeled Full) rather than hiding them
Show restricted sections, with the restriction spelled out
Remember the open tab and course between visits
Keep a course's color the same in every plan
Use Undo instead of “are you sure?” dialogs everywhere
answers.note: on the saturday point, usually this is actually a thing more often for async classes, which can have that same treatment. the registration limit is dependent on your major, so that's not necessary. people just screenshot things rather than save with image, that's not necessary.

answers.question: How the sidebar tabs look
answers.note: i definitely prefer this but it kind of reminds me of slack, which isn't good. for some reason apps that have this icon and rail thing with the grounded thing around it alaways seem to suck. maybe ours won't. i think this is *fine* for now. the text labels are very necessary i think, since most users are coming in blind.

answers.question: Hovering a search result
answers.note: this might actually be better than what i had mentioned before about allowing collapsible things for the distinction between two sorts of classes. ignore that, don't show sections in the main thing. but this hovering is awesome. and fills the need for comparing across upper levels.

answers.question: Search results
answers.note: i think maybe this should be a toggle in our search sections. you might be A) comparing sections within a course, like for a course with many sections or B) comparing sections across courses, like for upper levels with one section each and you're deciding between them.

answers.question: How a course's sections are listed
answers.note: this is a great idea. let's allow the user to collapse these instructor groups, too. i'd want to mostly preserve the number order of the sections though when we group. this is almost always the case with how they do the codes, though. just means not doing some extra sort on the instructor name or something like that.

answers.question: Opening a friend's shared link
answers.note: we're not doing overlays, so just a save a copy button. and we won't have names for this so can't say "Alex's plan" really. but i like this UI. what if we actually have it replace the list of our own plans at the top? of course with an X to go back and save a copy. i kind of like the current copy, icon, even the light red you're using here, maybe just put that up there in a little rounded sort of thing. just a thought.
